newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: EBRD MAKES FIRST INDUSTRY LOAN TO TAJIKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: EBRD MAKES FIRST INDUSTRY LOAN TO TAJIKISTAN.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Tuesday it had agreed to lend $1.7 million to a Tajik juice packaging joint venture in the bank's first industrial sector investment in the Central Asian country.
The loan agreement, with Khujand Packaging, was signed on Monday, senior EBRD banker Michael Delia told reporters.
"We are very excited about doing a project in Tajikistan, it is our first industrial project," he said.
The EBRD hopes the deal may be a model for other investments in the country, whose economy is in tatters after a lengthy civil war.
The joint venture, based in the northern city of Khujand, is being fornmed by the 60-year-old Khujand Canning Factory, Czech juice producer San Bravo and Austria's Oecko-Pack.
The joint venture will use new packaging equipment supplied by Austrian company PKL, which is contributing finance to cover project costs, whose total value is just less than $4 million.
Under the deal, the EBRD has the option to convert up to $250,000 of the principal into shares in the joint venture and bank officials said this was likely to happen.
"Very few people are making investments in this part of the world and if we can say it has been successful, we have a very good story," Delia said.
The money will be used to install and operate a friut and vegetable juice packaging plant. It will have planned annual production of 18 million litres.
Its main markets wil be Siberia and Kazakhstan but some juice will be heading for the Czech market.
